title: Recording opening: purpose of the Tulane interviews and Levy's birth
summary: The interviewer states the date and project and introduces Levy and Ike Robinson. Levy was born 14 November 1898 near Esplanade Avenue, New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: Bye-bye. This is January 3rd, 1961 and the subject of our interview is Mr. Charles Levy from New Orleans and you heard him read from his composition in the good old days in New Orleans. He didn't know that he was reading at the microphone but he was reading it to show me the spirit of some of the things he's written. voice besides mine and Mr. Levy's will be that of Ike Robinson who accompanied Mr. Levy today. The purpose of our tape or the purpose of the recording Mr. Levy is to provide the Tulane University with interviews, dictated sort and informal, relating to the New Orleans story. The Ford Foundation has provided Tulane with enough money that they can pay for the tape and we perform the interviews and they accumulate material for the history. I'd like to refer to them and learn something about your story. Would you like to take it for a little while? I kind of like to bring you into chronological stories. Sure, sure. When we were born and we were 1898 of all means. November 14th. And what part of you are? Oh, let's see. I think I was

born about a block from Esplanade Avenue, I think it was, on Barrick Street. Have you been back there lately? I haven't been there since 1914, but I said I want to go back. Oh, is that so? That's in my mind. I've seen the Monty Gras on TV and I'm telling you my heart almost cried. I'm telling you tears came to my eyes. I want to go back. Did you play when you were in LA? I was playing violin in a little group down there and just learning to put a little jazz in the violin, unbeknownst to my music teacher. Putting a
few extra notes in. Oh, we have a guy down there named Ernest Carrillo. And that guy was

way ahead each time. All right. I can hear you say something about the hearing and noise. It's a new microphone and it's possible if my contacts are bad, I'll go in there and see how they are. We may have to start over. But, go ahead with the story.
